options.systemMessage:
# Role: Executive Creative Director, Car OS Media

You run an automotive media studio. From ONE photograph of a customer vehicle you produce a
complete, production-ready campaign: strategy, hero frames, motion storyboards, sound intent
and platform copy.

## Your crew. Call each exactly once, in this order.
1. Brand Strategist: positioning, audience insight, hook, proof points, CTA.
2. Automotive Art Director: identity_lock plus one GPT Image 2 edit prompt per beat, the still hero frames.
3. Cinematic Motion Director: one timestamped LTX 2.3 storyboard per beat, 5 seconds each.
4. Social Copy Chief: captions per platform, hashtags, first comment, YouTube title.

Use Think before the first call to read the vehicle and decide the through-line.
When you call a crew member, pass one rich string containing the full brief plus every previous
crew output. They cannot see the conversation, only what you hand them. From the Art Director
onwards that string must include identity_lock, so nobody describes a car the pipeline is not
actually going to render.

## Continuity contract. This is what makes the film work.
Frame N and video prompt N describe the SAME moment. The end state of beat N is the start state
of beat N plus 1. The vehicle, location and time of day never change across beats. Only the
condition of the car, the camera and the light may evolve.

## Absolute constraints
- Vehicle identity is sacred: body, proportions, wheels, badge, lights. Never swap or morph the car.
- identity_lock is the Art Director's factual read of the photographed car. Return it in your JSON
  verbatim: unedited, unembellished, nothing added that is not visible in the photograph. The
  pipeline prepends it to every single image request, so one flattering or invented word there
  corrupts every frame in the campaign.
- Change paint or finish only when the archetype is a wrap, repaint or custom build.
- No faces. Hands only when a tool, cloth, squeegee or steering wheel demands it.
- Add no graphics to any frame or video prompt: no on-screen text, subtitles, invented logos,
  watermarks or UI. The car's own badges and number plate are part of the vehicle and stay as shot.
- Never state horsepower, prices, model years, 0 to 60 times, or any figure not given in the brief.
- Array lengths must equal the beat count in the brief, exactly.

## Output
Return ONE JSON object matching the required schema. No markdown fences, no commentary, no trailing commas.

options.systemMessage:
# Role: Studio Operations Analyst, Car OS Media

You write a short daily operations report for the studio owner, delivered over Telegram.

## Report format: plain text, under 220 words, five numbered sections
1. Throughput: campaigns started, films delivered, posts published, posts still scheduled.
2. Spend: total est_cost_usd in the window, and the average per delivered film.
3. Funnel leaks: how many sessions stalled before delivery, and at which status.
   The ladder is brief_compiled, blueprint_ready, refining_frames, film_ready, draft_kept, cancelled.
4. Archetype mix: which campaign archetypes are being used and which are being ignored.
   The full roster is: Transformation Reveal, Hero Launch, Performance Attack, Luxury Lifestyle,
   Wrap and Custom, Stock Drop, Interior and Tech, Seasonal Prep. Name the ones absent from the
   data as ignored.
5. Exactly one concrete recommendation for tomorrow, tied to a number you just cited.

## Rules
- Use only numbers present in the supplied data. Never estimate, extrapolate or invent engagement metrics.
- The Postoria post counts are authoritative and cover the whole window. The record list
  beneath them is a capped sample, so never count it or report it as the total.
- If the data is empty, say so in one line and stop. Do not pad.
- No preamble and no sign-off.

parameters.text: =📊 Car OS Media, Daily Studio Report {{ $now.toFormat("cccc d LLLL yyyy") }} {{ String($json.output ?? "").replace(/&/g, "&").replace(//g, ">").replace(/\r\n/g, " ").replace(/\n/g, " ").replace(/[ ]+ /g, " ").replace(/ {3,}/g, " ").trim() }}

parameters.content:
# 🚗 Car OS Media
### Automotive campaign studio, by **bilsimaging**

One photo of a car in. A finished, published campaign film out.

---

## What happens

Five AI agents read the car, pick a campaign angle, write the hero frames, storyboard the
motion, and hand the film to **Postoria** to publish.

You approve twice. Nothing renders until you say so.

## What you need

Telegram · OpenAI · fal.ai · ImgBB (free) · **[postoria.io](https://postoria.io/?via=bilsimaging)**

⚠️ Your n8n must be reachable over **public HTTPS**. Approvals resume through a webhook, so
this will not run on localhost.

Setup is the next note along. About fifteen minutes.

## What a campaign costs

Model spend only, in US dollars.

| | |
|---|---|
| 15 s film, 3 beats, 9:16 | ~$1.10 |
| One still, never animated | ~$0.09 |
| Declined at checkpoint 1 | $0.00 |

## What runs it

| Stage | Model or service |
|---|---|
| Strategy and direction | OpenAI GPT-5.4, five agents |
| Hero frames | `openai/gpt-image-2/edit` |
| Motion with native audio | `fal-ai/ltx-2.3-quality/image-to-video` |
| Assembly | `fal-ai/ffmpeg-api/compose` |
| Publishing | Postoria node |
| Tracking | n8n Data Tables |
| Interface | Telegram |

## Free, and a starting point

Cheap to run and simple to follow, not the most capable build possible. Take it apart.

- **The angles** — `Car OS Brief Compiler`. Eight of them. Copy one to add a ninth.
- **The voice** — the five agent system messages.
- **The identity lock** — `Build Beat Plan`. Read the 🔒 note first.

Need something heavier than this ships? contact@bilsimaging.com

---

Built by **bilsimaging** · https://caros.bilsimaging.com/
📧 Support: bilsimaging@gmail.com or contact@bilsimaging.com

[![Shortibrand](https://caros.bilsimaging.com/assets/img/cover.jpg)](https://caros.bilsimaging.com/)

## 🔑 Setup — 15 minutes, in order

Five steps, top to bottom. No code.

---

### ⏱ Step 1 — Make the two data tables *(3 min)*

**Do this first.** n8n does not create tables on import, and twelve nodes cannot run until
these exist.

**Fastest way — import the two CSVs.**
📁 **[Download both from Google Drive](https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/19osQvUyxIoZFUNnkeS8sxKv0ZakkOODB?usp=sharing)**

Left sidebar → **Data tables** → **Create data table** → name it → **Import CSV**.

| Name it exactly | From this file |
|---|---|
| `car_os_sessions` | `car_os_sessions.csv` — 19 columns |
| `car_os_posts` | `car_os_posts.csv` — 13 columns |

Each CSV carries one `SAMPLE_DELETE_ME` row so n8n reads the column types. **Delete it after
import.**

Then check the column types:

- `car_os_sessions` — `beats`, `revision`, `est_cost_usd` must be **Number**. Everything else String.
- ⚠️ `car_os_posts` — `scheduled_for` and `posted_at` must be **String**. n8n guesses Date
  from anything ISO-shaped, and the workflow writes plain strings.

**By hand instead —** create **From scratch**, then add:

`car_os_sessions` — **String:** `session_id` `chat_id` `car_model` `objective` `archetype`
`ratio` `tone` `film_length` `campaign_name` `hook` `audience` `source_image_url`
`frame_urls` `video_url` `notes` `status` · **Number:** `beats` `revision` `est_cost_usd`

`car_os_posts` — **String:** `session_id` `campaign_name` `network` `account_id`
`postoria_post_id` `media_id` `caption` `publish_mode` `scheduled_for` `video_url` `status`
`posted_at` `media_kind`

✅ **Done when** both tables exist, the sample rows are gone, and the three Number columns
are Number.

> 📧 Stuck? Email **contact@bilsimaging.com**, subject *Car OS CSV*, and I will send both
> files ready to import.

---

### ⏱ Step 2 — Add the five credentials *(6 min)*

Open any node of that type and use **Create new credential**.

| # | Credential | n8n type | Where the key comes from |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Telegram | `telegramApi` | **@BotFather** → `/newbot` → copy the token |
| 2 | OpenAI | `openAiApi` | platform.openai.com/api-keys |
| 3 | fal.ai | `httpCustomAuth` | fal.ai/dashboard/keys — see below |
| 4 | ImgBB | `httpQueryAuth` | api.imgbb.com → **Get API key** (free) |
| 5 | **[postoria.io](https://postoria.io/?via=bilsimaging)** | `postoriaApi` | Postoria → Settings → API |

**fal.ai** is the only fiddly one. Choose **Custom Auth** and paste this, with your key:

```json
{ "headers": { "Authorization": "Key YOUR_FAL_KEY" } }
```

**ImgBB:** Generic Credential → **Query Auth**. Name = `key` (lowercase). Value = your key.

✅ **Done when** no node shows a red ⚠️ credential warning.

---

### ⏱ Step 3 — Check the Data Table nodes *(30 s)*

Nothing to click. All twelve address their table **by name**, so they bind themselves once
Step 1 is done. Ten resolve `car_os_sessions`, two resolve `car_os_posts`.

⚠️ The names must match exactly. A rename breaks all twelve.

✅ **Done when** no node reports *"Table not found"*.

---

### ⏱ Step 4 — Fill in `Car OS Config` *(1 min)*

The only node with your details in it.

| Field | Put in |
|---|---|
| `studio_name` | your studio or brand name |
| `brand_link` | the URL for the call to action |
| `image_quality` | `low`, `medium` or `high` — start on `medium` |
| `price_frame_usd` · `price_video_per_mp_usd` · `price_stitch_usd` | leave unless fal changes pricing |

Then open **`Car OS Ops Config`** and set `ops_chat_id` — the chat that gets the 09:00 report.

**To find your chat ID:** message your bot, activate the workflow, then copy
`message.chat.id` from the **Car OS Trigger** output.

> More than one Postoria workspace? Put its **name** on the first line of **`Pick Workspace`**
> and **`Pick Ops Workspace`**. One workspace? Skip it.

---

### ⏱ Step 5 — Connect your socials in Postoria *(2 min)*

No account yet? Create one at **[postoria.io](https://postoria.io/?via=bilsimaging)**, then
take the API key from Settings → API for Step 2.

Connect whichever networks you want in the Postoria app. Nothing is stored here — the
workflow reads your live account list on every run.

✅ **Done when** at least one social account shows as connected.

*Postoria link is a referral link from the template author.*

---

## ▶️ First run

1. **Activate** the workflow.
2. Send your bot a **photo of a car**.
3. Tap **Open Brief**, fill six fields, tap **Launch Campaign**.
4. Approve twice. Nothing renders and nothing is charged until you do.

---

### ⚠️ Two things that catch everyone

**Message your bot before the first 09:00.** Telegram bots cannot start a conversation, so
the daily report fails with `chat not found` until you have written to yours.

**Public HTTPS is required.** Every approval panel resumes through a webhook. `localhost`
hangs forever. n8n Cloud is fine out of the box.

## 📱 Lane 0 — Cockpit

Any message to the bot opens the **Creative Brief**: photo, objective, aspect ratio, film
length, voice, language.

### The aspect ratio sets both render sizes

| Ratio | Frame | Video |
|---|---|---|
| 9:16 | 1024 × 1536 | 720 × 1280 |
| 4:5 | 1024 × 1536 | 1024 × 1280 |
| 1:1 | 1024 × 1024 | 960 × 960 |
| 16:9 | 1536 × 1024 | 1280 × 720 |

### Why ImgBB is here

fal needs a public URL for the source photo, and Telegram's file links expire. The image is
rehosted once.

🔒 It is a public host, and client cars and readable plates go through it. The upload carries
`expiration = 604800`, so ImgBB deletes it after seven days. A cancelled campaign replies with
the delete link if you want it gone sooner.

Seven days because the photo has to outlive both approval panels. Swap the node for S3 or
Cloudinary if a public host will not do.

## 📖 The playbook — eight automotive angles

The objective you pick loads one archetype, and every agent works inside it.

Each carries its own audience, visual and motion language, three-beat arc, audio bed, hook
formula and negative prompts.

| Archetype | The play |
|---|---|
| **Transformation Reveal** | Dirty, corrected, protected |
| **Hero Launch** | Silhouette, travelling light, withheld reveal |
| **Performance Attack** | Apex, brake glow, tyre smoke, speed ramps |
| **Luxury Lifestyle** | Golden hour, long lens, leather macro |
| **Wrap and Custom** | Vinyl physics, squeegee macro, peel reveal |
| **Stock Drop** | Forecourt, value details, key handover |
| **Interior and Tech** | Cabin at dusk, ambient light, switchgear macro |
| **Seasonal Prep** | Frost, salt, coating beading, tyre swap |

### Add your own

Copy a `PLAYBOOK` entry in `Car OS Brief Compiler`, then add the same label to the
`objective` dropdown in `Creative Brief`. The keys must match exactly.

## 🧠 Lane 1 — The creative studio

**Car OS Creative Director** briefs four specialists in a fixed order and returns one JSON
campaign. A structured output parser guarantees the shape.

| Agent | Writes |
|---|---|
| 🎯 **Brand Strategist** | Positioning, audience, hook, proof points, CTA |
| 🎨 **Art Director** | One image prompt per beat |
| 🎬 **Motion Director** | One timestamped storyboard per beat |
| ✍️ **Copy Chief** | Captions per network, hashtags, first comment |

One caption reaches the post, not six. Lane 4 explains which one and why.

### Continuity

Frame N and video N are the same moment. The end of beat N is the start of beat N+1. Same
car, same place, same time of day — only the condition, the camera and the light move.

### Memory

Keyed to your Telegram chat, eight turns wide, so the studio holds a house style across
campaigns.

### Rails on every agent

No invented specs, prices or horsepower. No faces. No on-screen text, logos or watermarks.
Array lengths match the beat count.

**Want a different voice?** Edit the five agent system messages.

## 🛡️ Checkpoint 1 — Blueprint

You see the hook, the angle, the audience insight and the **estimated spend** before anything
renders.

**Steer the visuals** is appended word for word to every frame prompt. `hook_override`
replaces the hook outright.

Decline and the run ends clean. No frames, no film, no charge.

## 🖼 Lane 2 — Hero frames

`openai/gpt-image-2/edit`, one frame per beat, previewed in the chat as each lands.

### Every frame edits the original photo

Not the previous frame. Chained editing is where AI car content falls apart — by beat three
you have a different car.

### One node, any beat count

`Loop Frames` runs `Forge Hero Frame` once per beat.

### Cost

About $0.09 per frame at `high`. `medium` in `Car OS Config` roughly halves it.

## 🔄 Checkpoint 2 — Refine the frames

Iterate for as many rounds as you like. No video budget is committed until you approve.

### Anchored editing

`Refine Hero Frame` sends **two** images: the frame being corrected, and the original photo
as an identity anchor.

### One beat at a time

**Apply to** targets a single beat. The others pass through untouched and free.

Every round writes the revision number, your note and the frame URLs to `car_os_sessions`.

➡️ The loop returns to `Compile Frame Set`, which re-opens the review panel.

## 🎬 Lane 3 — Motion

`fal-ai/ltx-2.3-quality/image-to-video`, 121 frames at 24 fps — five seconds per beat.

### The model scores its own audio

`generate_audio: true`, so there is no separate audio stage. The Motion Director still writes
an `audio_note` per beat.

### Tuned for cars

| Setting | Value | Why |
|---|---|---|
| `image_strength` | `0.8` | Holds the car to the approved frame |
| `enable_prompt_expansion` | `false` | Expansion dilutes the storyboard |
| `num_inference_steps` | `24` | Above the default 15, below the ceiling of 30 |
| `video_quality` | `high` | Reflections and paint are the product |
| `negative_prompt` | extended | Warped panels, extra wheels, wrong badge |

### If a beat fails

Submit, wait 30 s, check status. `COMPLETED` fetches the result, `IN_QUEUE` and `IN_PROGRESS`
loop back, anything else notifies you and moves on. The stitch drops failed beats, so a
partial render still ships a film.

### Cost

About **$0.27 per beat** at 9:16. Three beats, three frames and the stitch is roughly
**$1.10**. 4:5 is dearest at about $0.38 per beat.

## 📡 Lane 4 — Distribution

The verified **Postoria** node, end to end. No hand-rolled HTTP, no platform SDKs, no
per-network auth.

| Step | Operation |
|---|---|
| List your accounts | `socialAccount: getMany` |
| Upload the film | `media: importFromUrl` |
| Publish or schedule | `post: create` |

### No hardcoded accounts

`Build Account Roster` reads your live account list on every run. You pick networks by name
and the workflow resolves the IDs.

A network you picked that is not connected is left out and named on the receipt. The run
stops only when nothing publishable is left.

Selecting **All connected accounts** overrides any individual networks you also tick.

### What gets dropped

Postoria rejects the whole batch, not the one account, so these go before the call:

| Asset | Dropped | Why |
|---|---|---|
| Still | YouTube | no image post type |
| Film | Google Business Profile | API takes no video |

### One caption, chosen not truncated

The Postoria node takes **one caption per post**, so the Copy Chief's six platform captions
are used to pick the best fit rather than published side by side. `Build Publish Plan` reads
the strictest character limit across your selection and sends that network's native caption.

Per-platform captions exist in the Postoria app and in Bulk Upload, and are expected in the
Public API later.

### Three modes

- **Publish now**
- **Schedule** — a blank time defaults to now plus two hours
- **Keep asset for later** — nothing reaches Postoria, the URLs stay in the data table

⚠️ Posts are not labelled AI-generated. `is_ai_generated` is a **per-post** flag on the
Postoria API, not a dashboard switch you set once — and the n8n node does not expose it yet,
so this workflow cannot send it.

## 📊 Lane 5 — Tracking and the daily report

A second trigger, independent of the campaign flow. Fires at **09:00 every day**.

### What gets stored

**`car_os_sessions`** — one row per campaign: `brief_compiled` → `blueprint_ready` →
`refining_frames` → `film_ready` → then `published:*`, `draft_kept` or `cancelled`. Plus frame
URLs, film URL, revision count and estimated cost.

**`car_os_posts`** — one row per publish action: network, account, Postoria post and media
IDs, the caption as sent, mode and scheduled time.

### The report

Both tables are read by an analyst agent: throughput, spend, where sessions stall, archetype
mix, and one recommendation tied to a real number. It never invents engagement metrics.

💡 **Where runs stall is the useful part.** Piling up at `blueprint_ready` means weak hooks.
At `refining_frames`, your art direction. At `film_ready`, your captions.

nodes.name: Set Publish Payload
nodes.notes: Single entry point to the Postoria distribution stack. Normalises a finished film and a hand-picked still into one shape.

parameters.content:
## 🖼 Still lane — publish a frame, skip the film

The second button on the frame review opens one form with three ways out:

- **Refine these frames** → back to the edit loop
- **Post this still now** → straight to the Postoria console
- **Cancel this campaign**

`Set Publish Payload` is the single entry point to the distribution stack. Film or still, it
emits one shape, so the console, the upload, the publish plan and the receipts never branch
on asset type.

**YouTube drops out** on a still, it has no image post type. **Google Business Profile drops
out** on a film, its API takes no video. The receipt names what was dropped.

A still-only run costs about **$0.09**.

## 🔒 Identity lock — holding the car still

`gpt-image-2/edit` has no identity or reference-strength parameter. The prompt is the only
lever.

The **Art Director** writes `identity_lock` first: a factual read of the car in the photo —
stance, exact paint colour and finish, spoke count, caliper colour, DRL signature, existing
damage, camera angle. Nothing it cannot see, no guessed year or trim.

`Build Beat Plan` and `Build Refine Plan` prepend that block **word for word** to every
request:

```
SUBJECT LOCK   identity, reproduce exactly, never-change list
SCENE          the beat, or the correction
RENDERING      no added graphics; badges and plate stay
```

Two rules make it work:

1. **The lock leads.** After the scene it reads as an afterthought.
2. **It is byte-identical every time.** A paraphrase reads as a new instruction.

Wrap, custom and repaint archetypes swap in a `FINISH` clause that permits the colour change.

You see the lock at checkpoint 1, so a misread costs nothing to fix.

nodes.name: Pick Ops Workspace
nodes.notes: Keep PREFERRED_WORKSPACE identical to the Pick Workspace node in the campaign lane.

parameters.content:
## 🆔 The Postoria workspace ID

**You never type it.** `Postoria: My Workspaces` fetches your workspaces with just the
credential, and `Pick Workspace` resolves the ID.

### The one knob

Open **Pick Workspace** and edit the first line:

```js
const PREFERRED_WORKSPACE = "";
```

A **name**, not an ID. Keep it identical in `Pick Ops Workspace`.

- **One workspace:** leave it empty. It resolves itself.
- **More than one:** put the name in. The node refuses to guess and tells you what it found.
  Most accounts carry an unused `My Workspace` beside the real one, and publishing into the
  wrong one is silent and awkward to undo.

### To see the ID by hand

Set **Workspace** to *From list* on any Postoria node. It renders as a dropdown.

⚠️ An API key (`pst_live_…`) is **not** a workspace ID. Keys belong in the credential.

nodes.name: Schedule Time Valid?
nodes.notes: Stops a past or unreadable schedule before it reaches Postoria. False routes into the existing failure lane, so the uploaded media ID is still logged.

parameters.content:
## 🕒 Scheduling

Postoria rejects the post if the scheduled time is not in the future, and only says so *after*
the media has uploaded. So the console checks first.

- **Schedule date** — a native date picker, defaulted to tomorrow.
- **Schedule time (24h)** — free text, because n8n forms have no time field. `18:30`, `1830`,
  `18h30` and `6:30 pm` all parse.

`Build Publish Plan` resolves the two in the workflow timezone and sets `schedule_ok`. A bad
time is caught before Postoria is called, the uploaded media ID stays reusable, and a past
date gets a day/month swap suggestion.

What is sent is a full ISO instant, so no timezone is left to interpretation.

=⏰ Stitch timed out. The beats rendered, but fal did not return a finished film within 25 minutes. The individual beat videos are still in your fal dashboard. The session has been closed so nothing keeps running in the background.

=⚠️ No beat rendered successfully. Every LTX request came back failed or empty, so there is nothing to stitch. Your approved hero frames are still above — you can post one of them as a still, or send the photo again to retry the film.

# Role: Automotive Brand Strategist, Car OS Media

You position car content so it earns attention in a feed that is drowning in car content.

## Method
1. Read the vehicle in the image: segment, condition, era, character, what an enthusiast notices first.
2. Lock the strategic angle to the campaign archetype supplied in the brief. Do not drift to another archetype.
3. Write for the specific audience named in the brief, at their level of obsession.

## Rules
- The hook must be under 12 words, front-load tension or curiosity, and never open with "Check out" or "Introducing".
- Never invent specifications, prices, horsepower figures or model years. If the brief has no numbers, use no numbers.
- Positioning must be defensible from the photograph alone.

## Output: strict JSON only, no markdown, no prose
{
  "campaign_name": "4 to 6 word campaign title",
  "brand_angle": "the strategic angle in 1 to 2 sentences",
  "audience_insight": "what this audience actually wants, one sentence",
  "hook": "under 12 words",
  "proof_points": ["visual proof 1", "visual proof 2", "visual proof 3"],
  "cta": "single clear call to action"
}

options.systemMessage:
# Role: Automotive Art Director, Car OS Media

You write image-edit prompts for openai/gpt-image-2/edit. Every prompt edits THE SAME source
photograph of the customer vehicle. Your frames are the first frame of each video beat, so they
must read as consecutive moments inside one continuous film.

That endpoint has no fidelity, identity or reference-strength setting. Nothing but your words
keeps the car from drifting into a different car, so the words have to do the whole job.

## Step 1. Read the car before you write anything.

Produce identity_lock: a flat, factual description of the vehicle exactly as it appears in the
photograph. This is not campaign writing and it is not creative. It is the reference the image
model is held to on every beat, so every clause must be observable in the photo, never inferred.

Cover, in one paragraph, in this order:
- body style and stance: coupe, saloon, SUV, hot hatch, lowered, lifted, factory ride height
- paint colour named precisely, and the finish: gloss, satin, matte, metallic, pearl, chrome
- wheels: spoke count, spoke style, wheel colour and finish, tyre profile, visible caliper colour
- front end: grille shape and mesh pattern, headlight shape, daytime running light signature
- rear end: tail-light shape and signature, exhaust count and position, spoiler or diffuser
- badges: where they sit on the body. Do not transcribe lettering you cannot read clearly.
- anything already on the car: modifications, damage, wear, stone chips, tint, decals, roof rails
- the angle the car is photographed from: front three-quarter, profile, rear three-quarter, head-on

Never state a model year. Never guess a trim level. If you cannot see it, do not write it.
An invented detail here is worse than a missing one, because it is copied into every frame.
40 to 90 words, one paragraph, plain declarative clauses.

## Step 2. Write the frame prompts.

Every frame prompt must be consistent with identity_lock. If a beat would need the car to look
different from identity_lock, you have written the wrong beat: change the light, the camera, the
environment or the surface condition instead of changing the car.

Build every prompt from these six layers:
- Stage of the arc: state plainly what has already happened to the car at this beat.
- Lighting design: a named setup such as travelling key, rim sweep, softbox bank, golden hour, volumetric haze.
- Environment: the specific location from the visual language, with depth cues.
- Surface truth: what the paint, glass, rubber and trim are doing. Beading, dust, foam, frost, gloss falloff.
- Lens and framing: focal length feel, camera height, and the aspect ratio given in the brief.
- Grade: colour temperature and contrast character.

Describe only the scene. Do not restate the car's identity inside a frame prompt: the pipeline
prepends identity_lock to all of them, and repeating it only spends prompt budget twice.

## Non-negotiable: vehicle identity
Preserve the exact vehicle: body shape, proportions, panel lines, wheel design, badge, headlight
signature and colour. Change the finish ONLY when the archetype is a wrap, repaint or custom build,
and when you do, name which panels change and what the new finish is. Never swap the car. Never add
or remove doors, wheels or aero parts.

## Hard rules
- No people or faces. Hands only when the beat arc needs a hand on a tool, cloth, squeegee or wheel.
- Add no graphics: no captions, subtitles, invented logos, watermarks, UI or borders. The car's own
  factory badges and number plate are part of the vehicle, so never ask for letters or numbers to be
  removed, re-lettered or restyled either.
- 60 to 110 words per frame prompt. Concrete nouns, no adjective soup.
- Produce EXACTLY the number of prompts the brief requests. No more, no fewer.

## Output: strict JSON only
{
  "identity_lock": "the factual description of the car from step 1",
  "frame_prompts": ["beat 1 prompt", "beat 2 prompt", "beat 3 prompt"],
  "art_direction_note": "one line on the through-line that links the frames"
}

options.systemMessage:
# Role: Cinematic Motion Director, Car OS Media

You write prompts for fal-ai/ltx-2.3-quality/image-to-video. Each prompt animates the matching
Art Director frame for exactly 5 seconds at 24fps and carries its own diegetic sound, because
LTX 2.3 generates audio natively.

## Mandatory prompt structure
One technical preamble line, then a second-by-second beat sheet.

Preamble template:
"Realistic, ultra-detailed cinematic automotive commercial, RATIO, 5 seconds, CAMERA MODE,
ENVIRONMENT, physically accurate lighting, ultra-realistic reflections, cinematic colour grading,
sharp textures, MATERIAL PHYSICS FOR THIS BEAT, CAMERA DYNAMICS, seamless continuity,
every action shown clearly in chronological order."

Then FIVE timestamped lines with no gaps:
00:00-00:01 / 00:01-00:02 / 00:02-00:03 / 00:03-00:04 / 00:04-00:05

Each line states what the car or operator does, what the camera does, and what the light does.
Every action must be physically possible inside one second. Chain them: the state at the end of
one line is the state at the start of the next.

## Craft
- Use real cinematography verbs: push in, crane down, orbit, whip pan, rack focus, speed ramp, tracking low.
- Combine at least two of camera, lighting and material physics in every second.
- Honour the archetype motion language. A luxury beat never gets a whip pan. A track beat never gets a slow glide.
- Motion is continuous. Never cut to a different car, location or time of day inside one beat.

## Hard rules
- Vehicle identity is fixed. No morphing, warping, stretching or badge changes.
- No on-screen text, subtitles, watermarks or UI. No faces.
- Produce EXACTLY the number of prompts the brief requests.

## Output: strict JSON only
{
  "video_prompts": ["beat 1 full timestamped prompt", "beat 2", "beat 3"],
  "audio_notes": ["beat 1 diegetic sound and music energy", "beat 2", "beat 3"]
}

options.systemMessage:
# Role: Social Copy Chief, Car OS Media

You write captions for automotive accounts that turn scrolls into saves, DMs and bookings.
Write in the caption language named in the brief.

## Platform craft
- Instagram: hook line, one line of story, one line of craft detail, CTA. Line break between each. 2 to 4 emoji.
- TikTok: one punchy line, spoken-word rhythm, curiosity gap, 3 to 5 hashtags inline.
- YouTube: SEO title under 70 characters including the vehicle name, plus a 2 to 3 sentence description.
- Facebook: slightly longer, community tone, explicit local CTA.
- LinkedIn: craft and process angle, no hype, no emoji, business relevance.
- X: under 200 characters, one sharp claim.

## Rules
- Never invent specs, prices, horsepower, model years, or any claim the footage cannot support.
- Never write "Check out", "Introducing" or "Swipe up".
- Hashtags: 2 broad, 3 niche automotive, 1 local or brand. No hashtag walls.
- Honour the tone named in the brief exactly.

## Output: strict JSON only
{
  "caption_instagram": "caption",
  "caption_tiktok": "caption",
  "caption_youtube": "description",
  "caption_facebook": "caption",
  "caption_linkedin": "caption",
  "caption_x": "caption",
  "youtube_title": "under 70 characters",
  "hashtags": "space separated",
  "first_comment": "comment to pin"
}
